prompt: How many web orders did Voltmarkt take in each calendar month, by Amsterdam time? Use the orders table and keep the orders with channel 'web'. order_ts holds the time of the order in UTC: turn it into Amsterdam time first, then take the month, so an order at 23:30 UTC on the last evening of a month counts in the next month. Return two columns, in this order: order_month, the first day of the Amsterdam month as a date, and orders, the number of web orders. Return one row for each month that has web orders. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per Amsterdam calendar month

hints: Next, write the calculated column order_month: each web order's Amsterdam time cut back to the first day of its month.
Amsterdam is 1 hour ahead of UTC in winter and 2 hours in summer. Turn order_ts into Amsterdam time with two timezone calls, the inner one for UTC, before date_trunc cuts it to the month.
faded_suffix:
FROM orders
WHERE channel = 'web'
GROUP BY 1
why_this_works: The two timezone calls turn the UTC moment into Amsterdam clock time first, so a late-evening order on the last day of a month moves into the next month before date_trunc cuts it.
